requirements.title: BESSEL_YN arguments have integer-order and real-X restrictions
requirements.definition: N shall be of type integer and nonnegative; N1 and N2 shall be integer scalars with nonnegative values; X shall be real; for the transformational form X shall be scalar. X shall be greater than zero.

pending.bessel-yn-n-integer-nonnegative: Positive control uses initialized integer N = 2 in BESSEL_YN(N,X); noninteger or negative N variants are source-control negatives only because the unnumbered restriction is not a required diagnostic facet.
pending.bessel-yn-n1-integer-scalar-nonnegative: Positive control uses initialized integer scalar N1 = 2 in BESSEL_YN(N1,N2,X); noninteger, array, or negative N1 variants are source-control negatives only.
pending.bessel-yn-n2-integer-scalar-nonnegative: Positive control uses initialized integer scalar N2 = 4 in BESSEL_YN(N1,N2,X); noninteger, array, or negative N2 variants are source-control negatives only.
pending.bessel-yn-x-real: Positive control passes initialized real X to both BESSEL_YN forms; non-real X is a source-control negative only.
pending.bessel-yn-transformational-x-scalar: Positive control for the transformational form passes scalar X initialized to 1.0; an array-X transformational call is a source-control negative only.
pending.bessel-yn-x-positive: Positive controls use X = 1.0 so the greater-than-zero restriction is reached; zero or negative X variants are source-control negatives only because the unnumbered restriction is not a required diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: BESSEL_YN result characteristics match X and define the transformational extent
requirements.definition: The result has the same type and kind as X; BESSEL_YN(N1,N2,X) returns a rank-one array with extent MAX(N2 - N1 + 1, 0).

pending.bessel-yn-result-same-type-kind-as-x: Declare double precision X initialized to 1.0D0, compute both BESSEL_YN forms, and assert KIND(result) == KIND(X); initialized X avoids default-state vacuity.
pending.bessel-yn-transformational-rank-one: Compute BESSEL_YN(2,4,X) with scalar initialized X and assert RANK(result) == 1 before any element checks.
pending.bessel-yn-transformational-extent-max: Compute BESSEL_YN(2,4,X) and assert SIZE(result) == 3, then compute BESSEL_YN(5,3,X) and assert SIZE(result) == 0; both use initialized scalar X and avoid asserting approximate element values.

Description names the intrinsic Bessel function family.
Classifies the two-argument and three-argument forms.
Mixed result obligations and processor latitude for both cases are split into fine units.
